The views and opinions of authors expressed herein do not necessarily state or reflect those of the United States Government or any agency thereof. 2 Executive Summary Form Follows Function (F3): A Framework for Community-based Energy Resilience Planning in the Midwest led by the City of Duluth MN, is an innovative two-year initiative spanning August 1, 2023, to July 31, 2025. F3 created a replicable, human-centered energy resilience planning process specifically designed for smaller, cold-climate communities in the Midwest. F3 demonstrated both systems-level government planning and community-based research techniques to inform renewable investments and community preparedness strategies. The City of Duluth has faced multiple low-attention disasters including flooding, seiches, ice storms, derechos, and straight-line winds. The Form Follows Function project sought to address the challenges faced by smaller communities exposed to low-attention disasters, recurring minor events that often do not qualify for federal or state support but cumulatively cost billions. Although a major focus of the project was determining which municipal projects could produce “blue sky” financial and environmental benefits and maximize governmental investment in resilience, the project also addressed individual and shared community actions that could be taken to mitigate the negative impacts of grid outages as experienced by Duluth’s most vulnerable residents. The F3 planning approach included a Critical Infrastructure Team (CIT) and Community Stakeholder Group (CSG) to overcome limitations in traditional resilience planning, which often neglect population-based impacts and opportunities for decentralized approaches. The project methodology expanded organizational and individual knowledge of, and engagement in disaster preparedness. Through a collaborative approach, F3 ensured energy resilience planning was responsive to, and centered on, traditionally marginalized communities who are at the greatest risk of negative impacts from climate change and grid outages. F3 was originally aligned with potential federal programs, tax credits, and loan availability established by the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) to support resilience building at the critical systems, shared-community, and individual entity levels.
